ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZiMaDQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDJA0c", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 63, "title": "Implement retained S-3511A calendar and status for equipped cartridges", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `4b79ff5ac8612d50fc53f84fa27133f1e068efc3`, `crates/ws-core/src/bus.rs:436` always returns `0xFF` from RTC data port CB. Writes advance transport without updating a clock. Neither core/Wasm APIs nor browser persistence represent attached RTC state. Software therefore cannot set or retrieve a usable cartridge calendar. Commercial-title impact remains unmeasured.

Issue #53 fixed transport and explicitly deferred attachment, calendar and persistence. This task supplies those capabilities while retaining an explicit absent-chip configuration.

## Expected outcome

Supported equipped cartridges expose a progressing, retained S-3511A calendar and status through existing CA/CB polling. Restart and compatible model changes retain the clock while cancelling pending transport. The production browser restores the clock independently of SRAM, cartridge EEPROM and console EEPROM.

Scope includes attachment configuration, calendar/status/reset commands, controlled time, persistence, necessary adapter/player integration and automated regression coverage. Alarm/periodic interrupt delivery, cartridge IRQ wiring, factory firmware and broader mapper redesign remain separate material gaps.

## Context

Inspected local HEAD and remote main match the baseline. The open Issues/PR collection is empty; all 62 closed-work titles were checked. Relevant paths are `cartridge.rs`, `bus.rs`, `lib.rs`, `crates/ws-web/src/lib.rs`, `web/src/main.ts`, `web/src/saves.ts`, existing RTC tests and fixture/browser tooling.

Use the [manufacturer manual, §§2–4](https://abcelectronique.org/composants/telechargement_datasheet.php?id=836836&part-number=S-3511ASeries) for calendar, status, initialization and invalid-data behavior. Use pinned [libws routines](https://github.com/WonderfulToolchain/target-wswan-syslibs/blob/b3f2366c458421775cc4a18b4925d12a8d9c058b/libws/src/cart/cart_rtc.c) and [payload definitions](https://github.com/WonderfulToolchain/target-wswan-syslibs/blob/b3f2366c458421775cc4a18b4925d12a8d9c058b/libws/include/ws/cart/rtc.h) for host polling, preloaded writes, field ordering and masks. Preserve the independent [mapper experiment's](https://github.com/asiekierka/ws-test-suite/blob/5d8950d6b271a585c252af3ced93fbd2045f4752/src/mono/rtc/mapper/main.c) transfer expectations. Experiment source was inspected; no console pass log was inspected.

Correction record: the old assumption that footer byte 13 universally selects mapper hardware is unsupported. The pinned [swanlink producer](https://github.com/WonderfulToolchain/wonderful-i8086/blob/a77672a50369b0dfd6f646a8deedbf77c114c04e/support/swanlink.py) encodes its RTC indication there. The [original-board inventory](https://www.yaronet.com/topics/161842-hardware-type-de-pcb-cartouches-wonderswan) distinguishes RTC population from 2003 capability. Represent these independently. For the supported raw 00/01 convention, use 01 as the default equipped indication and provide an explicit absent override through core/Wasm/player configuration. Retain existing common/extended banking decisions as a documented compatibility policy, without claiming universal retail-board detection. This correction requires no human approval or independent AI re-review.

The [saved #61 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/4b79ff5ac8612d50fc53f84fa27133f1e068efc3/docs/issue-61-validation.md) reports native/build/browser passes and still requests final Coordinator review. Existing RTC tests are present but validate absent-chip transport. No builds or tests were run during this planning inspection.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Separate RTC presence from mapper capability. Exercise default equipped, explicit 2003-without-RTC and common-interface configurations. Preserve raw ROM identity, checksums, banking and independent diagnostics. Keep current SRAM capacities and existing save lengths unchanged; this task must not speculate about code-01 save migration.
- [ ] Implement reset, status and full/date-time-only transfers through CA/CB: BCD representation, 12/24-hour and AM/PM behavior, writable/reserved status masks, POWER handling, distinct cold initialization and explicit reset, and specified invalid-data correction. Both reset direction encodings reset the chip without treating the counted host byte as chip payload. Retain alarm configuration state where required by these registers; document that IRQ output remains unsupported.
- [ ] Preserve #53's literal command counts, terminal READY consumption, preloaded first writes, READY masking and labelled 64-clock stage approximation. Keep its complete `0xFF` expectations under explicit absent configuration, including the existing native and production-browser probe. Do not replace those assertions with equipped-clock expectations. Document unmeasured read-snapshot and interrupted-write phases as explicit policies before implementation.
- [ ] Provide deterministic injected time at the core boundary and production-browser synchronization independent of CPU/frame execution. Preserve fractional elapsed time; prevent double-counting host and emulated time. Define backward-clock handling without replaying elapsed intervals, and bound long offline catch-up without running corresponding game frames.
- [ ] Add independent literal vectors for second/minute/day rollover, 2024 leap day, common-year February, 30/31-day months, weekday wrap, 12-hour noon/midnight, 24-hour readback, status/reset and invalid fields. Document and test the two-digit-year boundary policy. Check equivalent partitioned time advances and no CPU/device advancement from host-clock synchronization alone.
- [ ] Retain completed RTC state across restart and compatible model changes; cancel pending transport without resetting retained time. Add validated core/Wasm export/import and a separately versioned browser-local record keyed by raw-ROM SHA-256, independent of console model and existing save records. Verify reopen/offline progression, cartridge isolation, absent-mode non-destruction, malformed/unsupported records, denied storage, failed imports and failed ROM loads without overwriting retained data.
- [ ] Cover emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations: Mono mode 00 and Color/SwanCrystal modes 00/80/C0/E0, including supported runtime round trips. Add an original source-included fixture using normal CPU IN/OUT polling. Assert CPU-written calendar/status results natively and through the production Chromium/Wasm player, including fresh restart and reopen. Inject time with automated tooling; preserve actual emulator execution and persistence. Invalidate stale pass records. Record at least one baseline CPU-level calendar/status failure and its corrected pass.
- [ ] Before merge, pass `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `git diff --check`. In `web`, pass `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against local production preview. Preserve CPU/interrupt/timing, graphics/input/frame, audio/PCM, GDMA/SDMA/Hyper Voice, SRAM/EEPROM, firmware-free startup, Wasm/browser lifecycle and ownership/provenance acceptance; require no proprietary ROM or firmware.
- [ ] Update hardware support, attachment/time/persistence policy, correction rationale, fixture provenance and validation documentation. Record actual failures, passes, final functional revisions and unperformed checks. The Coordinator must review every criterion and resolve blocking findings before merge. Keep unresolved retail detection, exact transport phases and alarm/IRQ behavior visible; do not claim broad commercial readiness.

## Optional validation

Additional browser engines or baseline browser discrimination. Console measurements and human gameplay are optional and were unperformed during planning. No device identity, physical-console run or human sign-off is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.

This autonomous campaign has no human-approval gate. Mandatory acceptance uses
automated native and production-browser tests on the emulator's supported model
and mode configurations. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are
optional evidence and must remain explicitly unperformed unless actually available.
Do not invent device identities, real-device results or a requirement for human
confirmation. Resolve technical errors with recorded evidence and automated checks
through the existing Coordinator workflow.
